# Khaggavisāṇa Sutta (Snp 1.3 (PTS Snp 6))

**ID:** Snp 1.3 (PTS Snp 6)
**Section:** Suttanipāta (snp)
**Collection:** Sutta
**Title (Pali):** Khaggavisāṇa Sutta
**tipitaka.org (CST):** https://tipitaka.org/romn/cscd/s0505m.mul0.xml

## AI-generated Overview (from reference literature)

*This overview was drafted by an AI model from the cited scholarship and catalog data and may contain errors; verify against the sources before relying on it.*

The *Khaggavisāṇa Sutta* is the third discourse of the *Uragavagga* in the *Suttanipāta* [Norman 1983]. Comprising a set of forty-one verses extolling the solitary life of an ascetic wanderer, nearly every stanza concludes with the renowned refrain advising one to "wander alone, like a rhinoceros horn" (*eko care khaggavisāṇakappo*) [Norman 1983]. Its core message is that if one cannot find a wise, suitable companion or teacher, it is preferable to wander alone rather than associate with fools. While the sutta itself gives no indication of its speaker, later canonical texts and commentaries ascribe the utterances to *paccekabuddha*s (solitary buddhas) [Kingsbury 2002; Norman 1983].

Scholars have noted the great antiquity and unique status of the discourse. The early canonical commentary *Cūḷaniddesa* comments on the *Pārāyaṇavagga* and this single poem, omitting the rest of the *Suttanipāta* [Hirakawa 1990; Buswell & Lopez 2014]. This indicates that the *Khaggavisāṇa Sutta* originally circulated as an independent, detached poem before the final compilation of the five-chapter *Suttanipāta* anthology [Hirakawa 1990; Hazra 1994; Buswell & Lopez 2014].

A full parallel is preserved in the Gāndhārī *Rhinoceros Sūtra* (GF 5B). In Pali canonical reuse, the entire 41-verse poem is cited and commented upon in the *Khaggavisāṇasuttaniddesa* (Cnd 23) and reproduced in the *Paccekabuddhaapadāna* (Tha-Ap 2) [Kingsbury 2002].

**Parallels and text reuse**

- Full parallels: GF 5B Rhinoceros Sūtra
- Passage-level parallels: dhp328; Mūlasarvāstivādivinaya (Gilgit III.ii.185); Ja 428 Kosambiyajātaka; MN 128 (PTS MN iii 152) Upakkilesa Sutta; P-Dhp 1–13 Jamavagga; Kd 10 Kosambakakkhandhaka; T 210.31 象喻品法句經第三十一十有八章; T 212.15 忿怒品第十五; T 213.14 法集要頌經怨家品第十四; UV 14 Drohavarga; Uv Kg 14 Hatred; MA 72 長壽王本起; Lzh Dg Kd 9 Kosambaka Khandhaka; dhp329; Thag 16.4 Raṭṭhapālattheragāthā; MN 82 (PTS MN ii 54) Raṭṭhapāla Sutta
- Resembling parallels: San Lo Mvu 33 The History of the Deer Park; Ja 12 Nigrodhamigajātaka
- Mentioned in: Cnd 23 Khaggavisāṇasuttaniddesa; Tha-Ap 2 Paccekabuddhaapadāna; Pe 2 Sāsanapaṭṭhānadutiyabhūmi

**Sources**

- [Norman 1983] K. R. Norman, Pali Literature (1983) — Details on the 41 verses, the recurring refrain, absence of named speakers, and commentary in the Cūḷaniddesa.
- [Kingsbury 2002] Paul Kingsbury, Chronology of the Pali Canon (2002) — Discussion of paccekabuddha attribution in Niddesa and Apadāna quotation (Tha-Ap 2).
- [Hirakawa 1990] Akira Hirakawa, History of Indian Buddhism (1990) — Analysis of the Niddesa's commentarial scope showing the sutta circulated before the five-chapter anthology took final form.
- [Hazra 1994] Kanai Lal Hazra, Pāli Language and Literature (1994) — Observations on the detached status of the Khaggavisāṇa Sutta prior to Suttanipāta anthology formation.
- [Winternitz 1933] Maurice Winternitz, History of Indian Literature, Vol. II (1933) — Parallel verses in the Mahāvastu and their context with five hundred dying Pratyekabuddhas.
- [Buswell & Lopez 2014] Robert E. Buswell Jr. & Donald S. Lopez Jr., Princeton Dictionary of Buddhism (2014) — Discussion of the Cūḷaniddesa's exegesis on Khaggavisānasutta and autonomous circulation.
